_comment: Small bundled subset of MITRE ATT&CK (Enterprise) technique descriptions used for lightweight keyword-overlap retrieval. Not exhaustive -- see mitre.org/attack for the full framework.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.text: Adversaries send phishing messages with malicious attachments or links to gain initial access. Macro-enabled office documents and encoded scripts are common delivery mechanisms.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.text: Adversaries abuse PowerShell for execution, often using encoded commands, hidden windows, or download cradles to retrieve and run a second-stage payload in memory.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task
techniques.text: Adversaries use the Windows Task Scheduler (schtasks.exe) to establish persistence by scheduling a malicious payload to execute repeatedly or at startup.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.text: Adversaries communicate with compromised hosts using HTTP or HTTPS to blend malicious traffic with legitimate web traffic, often via periodic beaconing to a command-and-control server.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.text: Adversaries dump credentials from memory (e.g. LSASS) or disk using tools such as Mimikatz to obtain account passwords or hashes for lateral movement.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.text: Adversaries proxy execution of malicious payloads through signed, trusted system binaries such as rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe, or mshta.exe to bypass application allowlisting.

techniques.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.text: Adversaries use valid credentials with tools like PsExec over SMB admin shares to execute code and move laterally between hosts on a network.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.text: Adversaries exfiltrate data over the same channel used for command and control, often disguised as ordinary web traffic to avoid separate detection.
